chapter: Chicago's South Side night life in the early 1920s
title: Leaving Chicago in February 1924 in the cold
summary: He left with Mamie Smith in bitter cold; they talk about Chicago winters.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well now, we've just got to recap a bit now on this last half hour. It seems to me that we did get out of Chicago a little bit quick. You did speak about -- but, of course, you -- yeah, you really left Chicago before it -- I mean you left Chicago so damn early, didn't you?

Yeah, it did. Since I left Chicago, yes, it did. I was there this past December visiting my (owns a house there) niece, nephew and my sister (unintelligible) South Chicago Avenue, stayed there a week, because I came there --
What time of year did you go there?
Oh, well, that's not -- that wasn't too bad, but if you have to go there in the realy wintry weather, I don't know how people stand that place.
Well, I tell you the truth. When I left there with Mamie Smith in February of 1924, it was so cold you couldn't see out of the taxicab windows (going out to the train station (unintelligible)).
Oh, I believe it. I mean --
-- you walk along, you turn a street corner, and the tears come out of your eyes.
-- you can't -- oh, I think that's an awful place. The winter --
That's why they call it the Windy city.
Rough place, right off that Lake Michigan.
